title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: Oil and gas price rises
sections.summary: Oil price has hit beyond US$100 per barrel and gas prices increased by more than 50% in one week, with more upside expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Oil price has hit beyond US$100 per barrel and gas prices as well had increased by more than 50% just last one week, and more price upside moves are expected.

sections.label: Singapore economy growth and inflation
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore can still grow 3% to 5% in 2022 as forecasted, and notes CPI expected between 2.5% and 3.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: All these grim developments paint a gloomy outlook for the Singapore economy, notwithstanding the 7.6% growth we registered in 2021, on the back of a 4.1% decline in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, can I ask the Minister if we would be able to still grow at 3% to 5% growth rate in 2022 as forecasted, or that the assumptions are no longer applicable and that we are back to the drawing board to determine a new forecast?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Of major concern is the impact on inflation, with CPI expected to range between 2.5% and 3.5%, based on earlier forecast.

sections.label: Job vacancies and worker retraining
sections.summary: An MOM report shows job vacancies hit over 98,000, a NTUC survey found 63% cited skills mismatch, and Budget 2022 set aside $100 million for training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, an MOM report shows that job vacancies have hit a record high of over 98,000, about double the running average.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A survey conducted by NTUC found that 63% of business leaders cited skills mismatch as the most prevalent form of mismatch but only 15% of these business leaders placed priority for retraining their workers to address the problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In Budget 2022, a sum of $100 million has been set aside to support NTUC in its efforts to upscale workers' training and businesses' transformation through the Company Training Committees (CTCs).

sections.label: Company Training Committees formed
sections.summary: Over 800 Company Training Committees have been formed since the initiative was launched in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Over 800 CTCs have actually been formed since the initiative was launched in 2019.

sections.label: Digital economy and green agreements
sections.summary: MTI designed the world's first digital economic agreement, with DEAs signed with several countries, and Grace Fu facilitated COP26 talks on Article 6.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is charting the way forward with these new engines of growth and MTI has taken the lead to frame and design the world's first digital economic agreement, DEA, and gotten us off to a fast start with DEAs signed with Chile, New Zealand, Australia, South Korea and, most recently, the UK.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the green front, Minister Grace Fu and her team played a key facilitation role at the UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP26), getting the world to agree on high-level talks to operationalise Article 6, which covers cooperation among countries to meet their emissions reduction targets, including through international carbon markets.

sections.label: Companies and staff trained
sections.summary: About 56 companies have participated with 165 staff trained, and Bosch Rexroth is applauded for retraining and reskilling staff for Industry 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To date, about 56 companies have participated with 165 of their staff trained and I applaud Bosch Rexroth for stepping forward to help themselves and the industry and, in so doing, get staff retrained and reskilled to be up to speed in Industry 4.0.

sections.label: SBF network overseas market landing
sections.summary: Over 3,000 companies are in the SBF network and 80 have landed overseas with signed distributorships or reseller contracts, with Market Readiness Assistance Grants available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to colleagues at SBF, today, more than 3,000 companies are part of this network and 80 companies have successfully landed in overseas markets with signed distributorships or reseller contracts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These companies leverage the network to take their aspiration for internationalisation one step forward and should these companies plan to go deeper and wider, they can apply for Market Readiness Assistance Grants from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This approach, no doubt is one company at a time, but, as the Chinese saying goes, "a thousand miles begin with a single step".

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, imagine my excitement to hear how Global Connect at SBF and the Singapore Food Manufacturers Association (SFMA) helped a few Singapore food brands to land in Vietnam together.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Map refresh progress
sections.summary: The Ministry was asked about the progress of the ITM refresh and whether it will address upskilling, retraining and hiring of mature and vulnerable workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Ministry previously mentioned that the Industry Transformation Map would be refreshed by this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What is the progress of the ITM refresh?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Will the ITM refresh consider workplace transformation and, specifically, address the upskilling, retraining and hiring of mature workers and other vulnerable workers for an inclusive transformation of the industries?

sections.label: Foreign labour for traditional sectors
sections.summary: The speaker says less competitive, traditional sectors should get more flexibility to tap foreign labour, limited to fields with severe Singaporean talent shortages and professionals aiding innovation, productivity, digitalisation or decarbonisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I expect that when the need for decarbonisation gains pace, professionals in those fields will also be in short supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is counter-intuitive, but the less competitive and more traditional sectors should be given more flexibility to tap into foreign labour, with the condition that it is only for fields where there is a severe shortage of Singaporean talent and only for professionals who will help the companies innovate, raise productivity, digitalise or decarbonise.

sections.label: Refreshed Industry Transformation Maps thrusts
sections.summary: Last year the Industry Transformation Maps were refreshed under a new five-year plan with three new thrusts: Emerging Stronger Taskforce recommendations, closer research and innovation integration, and greater focus on jobs and skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Last year, the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) were refreshed as part of a new plan over the next five years and included three new thrusts: incorporating the recommendations of the Emerging Stronger Taskforce, closer integration with research and innovation, and greater focus on jobs and skills.

sections.label: Singapore Global Enterprises initiative
sections.summary: In Budget 2022, Minister Lawrence Wong announced the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative to give bespoke support to promising larger local enterprises in innovation, internationalisation and partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: In Budget 2022, Minister Lawrence Wong announced a new initiative, the Singapore Global Enterprises, to provide bespoke support to promising larger local enterprises in areas of innovation, internationalisation and partnerships with other companies.

sections.label: SMEs find support options hard to navigate
sections.summary: Many SMEs appreciate the robust support but say the numerous offerings, from capability development and marketing to internationalisation capabilities, make available options difficult to navigate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Amongst the myriad of options, from capability development and marketing, to internationalisation capabilities at various stages of their development, many SMEs have provided feedback they are appreciative of the robust support but, due to the numerous offerings, they have found it difficult to navigate all available options.

sections.label: Support for tourism sector recovery
sections.summary: The passage asks about the Government's plan to support recovery of the hardest-hit tourism sectors, and notes firm deregistrations, new registrations, rising manpower costs, recruitment difficulties, and bank commitments to ease SME loan repayments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: What is the Government's plan to support the recovery of the hardest-hit sectors in tourism, given the prolonged impact of COVID-19 on the inflow of travellers?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Over the last two years, an average of around 3,840 firms were deregistered each month, similar to the period 2017-2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: On the other hand, an average of more than 5,000 new firms were registered each month over the last two years, reflecting an increase in the total number of businesses operating in Singapore, despite the impact of the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the same survey, 67.5% of respondents experienced rising manpower costs, including the cost of foreign workers, while 63.1% were unable to recruit local staff with the needed skills and 49.5% said that it has become more difficult to get foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Banks and finance companies in Singapore have committed to help ease the financial strain on SMEs arising from the need to make principal repayments on their loans during this period, in view of the temporary cashflow constraints that many face.

sections.label: Code of conduct for fair tenancies
sections.summary: Industry associations developed a code of conduct for fair tenancies during COVID-19, and the passage seeks updates on its rollout and confirmation that all Government landlords adopted it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, during the COVID-19 pandemic, various industry associations, such as Singapore Business Federation (SBF), Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME), Restaurant Association of Singapore (RAS), Singapore Retailers Association (SRA), Singapore Tenants United for Fairness (SGTUFF), Real Estate Developers' Association of Singapore (REDAS) and REIT Association of Singapore (REITAS) had come together to develop the code of conduct for fair tenancies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Such a code of conduct provides a fairer tenancy agreement outcome for all parties which sets the basis for business survivability and sustainable growth for both landlords and tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, I would like to seek updates on the rollout and implementation of the code of conduct for fair tenancy and can I confirm that all Government landlords have adopted this framework?

sections.label: Timeline for legislating tenancy code
sections.summary: The passage requests a timeline towards legislating the code of conduct for fair tenancies into law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Fourth, I would like to request a timeline towards legislating this code of conduct into law.

sections.label: TACs coordinating shared services
sections.summary: The passage states TACs can coordinate shared services for members to get favourable rates and economies of scale, and suggests Enterprise Singapore could adapt the Enterprise Development Grant for mass funding, citing the SG United Training scheme administered by SBF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, TACs can coordinate shared services for their members that would help them get favourable rates and enjoy economies of scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, Enterprise Singapore could consider adapting the Enterprise Development Grant in a way that would allow TACs to coordinate mass funding for their members in the eligible areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A good recent example is how the SG United Training scheme is administered by the Singapore Business Federation.

sections.label: Extending grants to TACs
sections.summary: The passage asks MTI if it will consider extending grants traditionally offered to SMEs to TACs to help them build revenue making activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask MTI if it will consider extending grants to TACs that are traditionally offered to SMEs to help them build revenue making activities.

sections.label: TACs encouraging knowledge sharing
sections.summary: The passage states TACs can encourage knowledge sharing among members, and asks MTI how it can better incentivise and equip TACs to step up these efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: TACs can also play a role in encouraging knowledge sharing amongst their members, so that businesses can learn about successes and pitfalls faster in their journey for growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, can MTI share how it can better incentivise and equip TACs to encourage them to step up their efforts in this area?

sections.label: SME energy price support measures
sections.summary: The passage asks what short-term measures the Government will provide for SMEs facing higher energy prices and whether TRECS will be extended to all SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While the business support packages in Budget 2022 are generous and with digital transformation, productivity and trading schemes, can the Minister explain what short-term measures will the Government further provide for SMEs to cope with the yet higher energy prices?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider further extending the availability of the Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme (TRECS) to all SMEs which wish to subscribe, given that it is reviewed monthly?

sections.label: Reviewing demand aggregation openness
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the demand aggregation model can be reviewed to improve openness and enhance business competition for Government contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As the digitalisation of procurement processes has made it efficient, can the demand aggregation model be reviewed to improve openness so as to enhance business competition for Government contracts?

sections.label: Six hundred million dollars set aside
sections.summary: The passage states that six hundred million dollars have been set aside to help them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Six hundred million dollars have been set aside to help them.

sections.label: Singapore business R&D expenditure and commercialisation
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's business R&D expenditure lags other economies, most R&D is MNC-driven, and more investment seeks private sector collaboration with 80 research centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Singapore's total business R&D expenditure lags behind other economies, with most of the nation's R&D efforts driven by MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We are investing more into R&D, seeking to boost the private sector's collaboration with 80 research centres islandwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The value from innovative ideas generated from R&D must be captured in a timely fashion and commercialised for businesses to fully benefit from R&D efforts.

sections.label: CCCS injunction orders against errant businesses
sections.summary: The passage states that since the 2016 CPFTA amendments, CASE referred 10 businesses to CCCS, which obtained three injunction orders, taking about 20 months each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since the last CPFTA amendments in 2016, CASE has referred 10 businesses to CCCS for investigation and CCCS has successfully obtained three injunction orders against these errant businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But, Sir, it took CCCS about 20 months to obtain an injunction order to stop these businesses and to stop their unfair practices.

sections.label: CCCS financial penalties for egregious cases
sections.summary: The passage states that for egregious cases, MTI should empower CCCS to impose financial penalties on errant businesses without first obtaining a court injunction order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: For egregious cases, MTI should empower CCCS to impose financial penalties on errant businesses without having to first obtain an injunction order from the Courts.

sections.label: Beauty contracts cooling-off period
sections.summary: Including beauty-related contracts as regulated contracts gives consumers a five-day mandatory cooling-off period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Including beauty-related contracts under the ambit of regulated contracts will provide consumers with a crucial five-day mandatory cooling-off period.

sections.label: 2021 economic recovery
sections.summary: Singapore grew 7.6% in 2021, with strong growth in several sectors and $11.8 billion in Fixed Asset Investment commitments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Together, we achieved a strong recovery last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We rebounded from the worst recession since Independence, growing by 7.6% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In particular, the manufacturing, information and communications, finance and insurance and wholesale trade sectors recorded strong growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We also remained attractive to global investors, securing commitments of $11.8 billion in Fixed Asset Investment and $5.2 billion in Total Business Expenditure in 2021.

sections.label: Small Business Recovery Grant
sections.summary: The Finance Minister announced a Small Business Recovery Grant of $1,000 per local employee, up to $10,000 per firm, for sectors most affected by COVID-19 restrictions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister announced that we will be supporting firms in sectors which have been most affected by COVID-19 restrictions, through a Small Business Recovery Grant (SBRG) of $1,000 per local employee, up to $10,000 per firm.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore transformation support
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore supported over 22,000 enterprises in transformation efforts last year, a 44% increase from the year before.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Last year alone, Enterprise Singapore supported over 22,000 enterprises in their transformation efforts, an increase of 44% compared to the year before.

sections.label: Manufacturing 2030 and semiconductor sector
sections.summary: Manufacturing 2030 aims to increase manufacturing value-add by 50% in 10 years; the sector grew 13.2% and received $8.5 billion in Fixed Asset Investment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, we account for 11% of the global semiconductor market and 20% of global semiconductor equipment is manufactured in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked for an update on our Manufacturing 2030 vision and the opportunities in this sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We launched Manufacturing 2030 last year, with the aim of increasing manufacturing value-add by 50% in 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Last year, the sector grew very significantly by 13.2% and received $8.5 billion in total Fixed Asset Investment, creating over 6,000 jobs when these projects are completed.

sections.label: Plant-based food growth projection
sections.summary: Plant-based food is projected to grow by 100 times by 2050 across the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Plant-based food, for example, is projected to grow by 100 times by 2050 across the world.

sections.label: Manufacturing 2030 ambitions
sections.summary: Efforts will be redoubled to grow a vibrant core of Singapore Global Manufacturers that are deeply innovative.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To make a further push towards our Manufacturing 2030 (M2030) ambitions, we will redouble efforts to grow a vibrant core of Singapore Global Manufacturers that are deeply innovative and can deliver distinctive offerings to their customers.

sections.label: M2030 Careers Initiative launch
sections.summary: The M2030 Careers Initiative will work with industry to offer career progression pathways, targeting polytechnic and ITE graduates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To do so, companies need to offer attractive career progression pathways in line with technological changes and ensure these prospects are accessible and exciting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will therefore launch the M2030 Careers Initiative to work with the industry to achieve this, targeting especially our graduates from the Polytechnics and the Institute of Technical Education (ITE), who have been trained with industry-relevant skills.

sections.label: ITE internship opportunities
sections.summary: Work with companies aims to secure at least 200 ITE internship places from 60 companies by end of 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are also working with companies to offer additional high-quality internship opportunities for students in the ITE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We aim to secure at least 200 places from 60 companies by the end of 2022.

sections.label: APT(M) Grant pilot
sections.summary: Selected companies will pilot the Accelerated Pathways for Technicians and Assistant Engineers Grant for Manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I look forward to more of such conversion stories in the near future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will also work with selected companies to pilot the Accelerated Pathways for Technicians and Assistant Engineers Grant for Manufacturing, or APT(M) Grant.

sections.label: Trade 2030 strategy
sections.summary: Trade 2030 aims to grow export value from $805 billion to at least $1 trillion and double offshore trade value by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Second, we will embark on a Trade 2030 strategy to grow our trading volume, widen the types of trading activities in Singapore and expand trade with other parts of the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: From 2020 to 2030, we aim to grow our export value from $805 billion to at least $1 trillion and double our offshore trade value from US$1 trillion to US$2 trillion.

sections.label: Trading sector employment
sections.summary: The trading sector had over 300,000 employees in 2020, mostly locals, with close to 70% PMET jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The trading sector is one of Singapore's largest employers with over 300,000 employees in 2020, of which the majority are locals and close to 70% are PMET jobs.

sections.label: Enterprise 2030 strategy for local businesses
sections.summary: Singapore will embark on an Enterprise 2030 strategy to identify and support promising local businesses, including through the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These enterprises will then create new jobs and meaningful careers for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will therefore embark on an Enterprise 2030 strategy, to scale up efforts to identify and support promising local businesses, including through the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative to support their growth into global champions.

sections.label: Studio transformation with union and NTUC
sections.summary: A company worked with CMPU and NTUC on an Operations Technology Roadmap and three-year workplan, then grew its business and hired 13 additional staff.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The company worked with its union – the Creative Media and Publishing Union, or CMPU, and the NTUC Training and Placement ecosystem to conduct an Operations Technology Roadmap, and developed a three-year workplan to transform its business and workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The studio has since grown its business and hired 13 additional new staff, some of whom are interns and SGUnited Trainees.

sections.label: Ukraine conflict and recovery outlook
sections.summary: The Ukraine conflict will add bumps to recovery, but Singapore must build on fundamentals, strengthen agility and make short-term adjustments for long-term dividends.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The conflict in Ukraine will add bumps on our road to recovery and growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: But let us look ahead into the future with confidence and resolve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will need to work hard to build on our strong fundamentals, strengthen our agility to respond to uncertainties and amass the fortitude to make adjustments that can be painful in the short run, but will pay handsome dividends in the long run.

sections.label: Cultivating Singapore Global Enterprises
sections.summary: An initiative will be launched to cultivate a new generation of Singapore Global Enterprises that are locally grown and globally competitive.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To do so, we will launch an initiative to cultivate a new generation of "Singapore Global Enterprises" which are locally grown and globally competitive.

sections.label: Singapore Global Executive Programme launch
sections.summary: The Singapore Global Executive Programme will be launched to boost human capital capabilities of high potential local enterprises and support talent attraction, retention and leadership succession.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa have pointed out, the answer lies in "growing our own timber", providing the space and opportunity to nurture and support Singaporeans to be part of the growth stories of many more promising enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will launch the Singapore Global Executive Programme (SGEP) to boost the human capital capabilities of our high potential local enterprises and support them in talent attraction and retention, as well as leadership succession programmes to develop a pipeline of future leaders, not just locally, but globally.

sections.label: EDB M&A grant and growth funds
sections.summary: EDB will launch a Mergers and Acquisitions grant to co-fund qualifying spend on advisory services, and three funds were launched to provide capital and fundraising options.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To help our enterprises on this journey, EDB will be launching a Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) grant to co-fund the qualifying spend on Singapore-based professional and financial advisory services incurred on the M&A deal.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have also launched three funds recently to provide capital to accelerate the growth of our enterprises, broaden the range of fundraising options and help them work towards an eventual public listing or liquidity event in Singapore.

sections.label: Government funding for projects
sections.summary: Since 2010, the Government has set aside over S$150 million for projects benefiting more than 2,000 Singapore-based companies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Since its inception in 2010, the Government has set aside more than S$150 million to support these projects which have benefited over 2,000 Singapore-based companies.

sections.label: Firms benefiting from initiative
sections.summary: More than 80,000 firms have benefited from the initiative since its 2017 launch.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: More than 80,000 firms have benefited from the initiative since it was launched in 2017.

sections.label: RIE 2025 research investment
sections.summary: Under RIE 2025, investments in research, innovation and enterprise will be sustained at 1% of GDP, or $25 billion, from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Under our RIE 2025 plan, we will sustain investments in research, innovation and enterprise at 1% of Singapore's GDP, or $25 billion, from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: Fortitude COVID-19 test kit development
sections.summary: A*STAR's EDDC, the Diagnostics Development Hub and Tan Tock Seng Hospital developed the Fortitude COVID-19 test kit, the first lab diagnostic kit to receive HSA Provisional Authorisation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the fight against COVID-19, the A*STAR's Experimental Drug Development Centre (EDDC) collaborated with the Diagnostics Development Hub and Tan Tock Seng Hospital to develop the Fortitude COVID-19 test kit, the first lab diagnostic kit to receive Provisional Authorisation from Singapore's Health Sciences Authority (HSA) for clinical use.

sections.label: Energy security measures amid Ukraine conflict
sections.summary: MTI and EMA have put in place measures including fuel reserves, a Standby Fuel Facility and TRECS, extended from March to May 2022, to safeguard energy security and help consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: While Singapore's sources of fuel are diversified and the conflict in Ukraine poses limited direct risks to our supplies, we will be affected by the high or volatile global gas prices arising from the conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As the Minister for Trade and Industry and I have explained in this House, MTI and EMA have put in place various measures to safeguard energy security and to help consumers cope with rising electricity costs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These include ensuring that generation companies have sufficient fuel reserves, establishing a Standby Fuel Facility which generation companies can tap on to produce electricity and working with the generation companies and electricity retailers to offer fixed price contracts under the Temporary Retail Electricity Contracting Support (TRECS) scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: EMA is also working with them to offer longer term fixed price contracts to consumers who wish to have more price stability.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have since extended TRECS from March to May 2022 and we will extend it further if necessary.

sections.label: Tech.Pass and Tech@SG schemes
sections.summary: Tech.Pass and Tech@SG were launched to give firms access to specialised talent, with around 180 Tech.Pass holders and more than 50 firms on Tech@SG.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For example, we had recently launched specific schemes, such as the Tech.Pass and Tech@SG to provide firms with access to specialised talent.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These schemes have been well-received by companies, with around 180 Tech.Pass holders and more than 50 firms on Tech@SG.

sections.label: Enterprise transformation and future economy
sections.summary: The Government urges enterprises to transform and become Singapore Global Enterprises, and will continue supporting them.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Importantly, we will need to continuously innovate, think outside the box and transcend our own physical boundaries and constraints to seize the opportunities of the future economy.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I strongly urge and encourage our enterprises to equip themselves for the future, press on with transformation and set their sights to become the next Singapore Global Enterprise.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to support them in this journey.

sections.label: Enterprise Financing Schemes financing
sections.summary: In the last two years, close to 28,000 companies secured financing from the Enterprise Financing Schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In the last two years, close to 28,000 companies have secured financing from the Enterprise Financing Schemes (EFS).

sections.label: EFS M&A Programme expansion
sections.summary: The EFS M&A Programme will be expanded to include domestic M&A activities from 1 April this year to 31 March 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To support more companies like GKE in their growth plans, we will be expanding the EFS M&A Programme to include domestic M&A activities from 1 April this year to 31 March 2026.

sections.label: GoBusiness portal usage
sections.summary: As of January 2022, close to 43,000 businesses used GoBusiness to apply for assistance and over 56,000 benefited from e-Advisers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As of January 2022, close to 43,000 businesses have used the GoBusiness portal to apply for Government assistance, and over 56,000 have benefited from the e-Advisers' personalised recommendations.

sections.label: Small Business Recovery Grant
sections.summary: The Small Business Recovery Grant will provide up to $10,000 per firm in the most affected sectors to help SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The Small Business Recovery Grant (SBRG) will provide up to $10,000 per firm in the most affected sectors to help these SMEs regain their footing and build back their strength.

sections.label: Food services and retail revitalisation package
sections.summary: A $70 million Food Services and Retail Business Revitalisation Package will be introduced, extending 80% EDG and PSG support till 31 March 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Today, I am happy to announce that we will be introducing the $70 million Food Services and Retail Business Revitalisation Package to help our food services and retail companies overcome these challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The new Food Services and Retail Business Revitalisation Package will: one, extend crucial support for our businesses in these sectors to improve their productivity and equip them with the capabilities to pivot and transform, so as to stay competitive and relevant; and two, help our food services and retail companies to beef up their manpower in the hiring and training of locals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Hence, we will extend the 80% support level of the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) and relevant solutions under the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) for the food services and retail sectors till 31 March 2023.

sections.label: EDG project cost savings
sections.summary: The company estimates three EDG projects saved it at least $60,000 per month on operating costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The company estimates that these three EDG projects have saved them at least $60,000 per month on operating costs.

sections.label: SingapoRediscovers Vouchers scheme results
sections.summary: The SRV scheme generated nearly $300 million in SRV-related bookings and transactions and up to $100 million in ancillary spending.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Members will remember the SingapoRediscovers Vouchers (SRV) scheme last year, which generated nearly $300 million in SRV-related bookings and transactions and up to $100 million in ancillary spending.

sections.label: Singapore Air Show 2022 attendance
sections.summary: Singapore Air Show 2022 welcomed an estimated 13,000 trade attendees and almost 600 exhibitors from over 39 countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I think Members will remember, just two weeks ago, the Singapore Air Show 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: It welcomed an estimated 13,000 trade attendees and almost 600 exhibitors from over 39 countries.

sections.label: STB and WSG tourism company support
sections.summary: Over two years, STB and WSG supported over 140 tourism companies through various CCPs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Over the last two years, STB and Workforce Singapore (WSG) supported over 140 tourism companies through various CCPs.

sections.label: SCCCI and SBF TAC outreach
sections.summary: SCCCI and SBF aim to reach at least 150 TACs to upskill secretariats, raise capabilities and add value to business members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Through this initiative, SCCCI and SBF aim to reach out to at least 150 TACs on upskilling their secretariats, to raise TACs' capabilities and to add value to their business members.

sections.label: CAP investigating unjustified GST price rises
sections.summary: CAP will investigate businesses that unjustifiably raise prices of essential products and services using the GST increase as an excuse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I am grateful that many Members of the House welcomed the aims and the work of the CAP that Minister Lawrence Wong announced during the Budget two weeks ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I want to assure Mr Sharael Taha that CAP will investigate businesses that raise prices of essential products and services unjustifiably using the GST increase as an excuse.

sections.label: Heartland enterprises digital channels
sections.summary: 58% of heartland enterprises, about 9,900, are onboard digital channels and e-commerce platforms and have Google My Business pages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In fact, more than half – 58% of our heartland enterprises and that translates to about 9,900 heartland enterprises – are now onboard digital channels and onboard e-commerce platforms such as Carousell, Fave, Shopee and have set up a Google My Business page to create an online presence.

sections.label: Our Heartlands 2025 initiative
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will launch Our Heartlands 2025, estimated to cost about $50 million, aiming for nine in 10 shops to adopt a digital solution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will be launching a new initiative called Our Heartlands 2025, which we estimate will cost about $50 million to help our heartland enterprises increase revenue, improve their operational efficiency thereby reducing cost and expand their customer base both online and offline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Mr Shawn Huang will be glad to note that under Our Heartlands 2025, we aim to further expand our digitalisation efforts, so that nine in 10 shops will adopt at least one digital solution.

sections.label: Secretariat training and shared secretariat
sections.summary: This involves training secretariats in project management, precinct rejuvenation and financial management, and supporting FMAS in launching a shared secretariat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This will involve training their secretariat in aspects such as project management, precinct rejuvenation and financial management.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We will also support FMAS in launching a shared secretariat for local merchants' associations.

sections.label: CDC vouchers distribution and claims
sections.summary: Three tranches totalling up to $650 million in CDC vouchers will be distributed over 2022 to 2024, with 90.6% of households claiming the first tranche.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The Government recently committed another three tranches, which total up to $650 million in CDC vouchers, which will be distributed over 2022 to 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To date, more than 1.1 million Singaporean households, which translate to 90.6% of households, have claimed the first tranche of $130 million CDC vouchers and $62 million worth of CDC vouchers have been spent in the last three months.

sections.label: Food Services and Retail Revitalisation Package
sections.summary: A $70 million Food Services and Retail Revitalisation Package will be introduced to help businesses seize growth opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We also recognise that some sectors may need additional assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We will be introducing the $70 million Food Services and Retail Revitalisation Package to help businesses seize growth opportunities.

sections.label: Our Heartlands 2025 programme aims
sections.summary: The $50 million Our Heartlands 2025 programme aims to deepen merchants' associations' capabilities and help heartland shops adopt technology and digitalise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The $50 million Our Heartlands 2025 programme aims to deepen the capabilities of merchants' associations and help heartland shops adopt technology and digitalise.

sections.label: COVID-19 opening up and recovery
sections.summary: Numbers have stabilised over the last few days, possibly nearing the peak, but anything could happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, on COVID-19 and our progress for opening up and our economic recovery efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I should first clarify that while the numbers have stabilised over the last few days, which may suggest that we are probably nearing the peak, but anything could happen.

sections.label: Workers returning to work
sections.summary: It is important to progressively allow workers to go back to work, with 50% of employees required to work from home where practicable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Second, it is important to progressively allow workers to go back to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So far, we have a requirement for 50% of employees to work from home, where practicable.

sections.label: Economic recovery and CPTPP
sections.summary: Three aspects will be looked at to allow the economy to continue recovering, and Singapore will chair the CPTPP Commission this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: These are the three aspects which are very important and we will continue to look at these to allow the economy to continue on its journey of recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This is a very important agreement that we have entered into and this year Singapore will be chairing the Commission for CPTPP.

sections.label: US and Indo-Pacific economic talks
sections.summary: Discussions with the Department of Commerce cover initiatives for businesses and a possible Indo-Pacific Economic Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are in the midst of a discussion with the Department of Commerce on how we can take this further in introducing initiatives to encourage businesses on both sides to tap on opportunities in each other's countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are also discussing the possibility of establishing an Indo-Pacific Economic Framework to allow collaboration among Indo-Pacific economies.

sections.label: FTA utilisation rates
sections.summary: The average utilisation rate for all FTAs Singapore has signed is asked about, citing Singapore-US FTA at 15% and Korea-Singapore FTA at 8%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I wonder if he is able to share in terms of the average utilisation rate for all the FTAs that Singapore has signed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I ask this because, based on the available data, I see that, for example, the Singapore-US FTA's utilisation is only at 15%, the Korea-Singapore FTA is 8%.

sections.label: Services share of exports
sections.summary: Services trade constitute about 40% of Singapore's total exports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Services trade constitute about 40% of our total exports.

sections.label: tariff savings amount
sections.summary: The tariff savings constituted about $1 billion last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The tariff savings constituted, I think if I remember correctly, about $1 billion last year.

sections.label: public-private partnership PACT
sections.summary: PACT has been started with regard to public-private partnership.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With regard to public-private partnership, we have started PACT, as I have said earlier on.

sections.label: ITM business job worker changes
sections.summary: Remodelling businesses, redesigning jobs and retraining workers are integral parts of the ITM journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In the process of redesigning the jobs, we need to train the workers so that they are able to take on these new jobs that have been redesigned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, remodelling of the businesses, redesigning the jobs and retraining of the workers are actually integral parts of the entire ITM journey.

sections.label: Budget funds for CTP
sections.summary: A question asks whether this year's Budget sets aside any amount for enhancements to the CTP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can Minister explain further, whether in this year's Budget, whether there is any amount set aside for enhancements to the CTP?

sections.label: eurozone impact on Singapore businesses
sections.summary: A question asks about plans and concerns to help businesses exposed to the eurozone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The impact on eurozone growth is a big concern now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, from an economic growth perspective and its impact on businesses in Singapore, what are our plans and concerns to help businesses, especially those that are exposed to eurozone?

sections.label: beefing up Company Training Committees
sections.summary: The Finance Minister announced that Company Training Committees will be significantly beefed up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Finance Minister had also announced that we will be significantly beefing up the Company Training Committees (CTCs).

sections.label: Ukraine conflict food supplies
sections.summary: The Ukraine-Russia conflict affects supplies from Ukraine and Russia, but Singapore has diversified supplies and sufficient basic food commodities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: With the conflict between Ukraine and Russia, supplies from Ukraine and Russia, particularly Ukraine, would be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, we do have some imports from Ukraine, but we have diversified supplies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We do have sufficient supply of basic food commodities.

sections.label: Flights, supply chains, higher costs
sections.summary: Flights are affected, and supplies and supply chains will lead to higher costs, which Singapore cannot insulate itself from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Flights are already affected, as all of us know.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, one is supplies; second, supply chains; and third, both of these will lead to higher costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Singapore, being an open economy, we will not be able to insulate ourselves from all these impacts.

sections.label: CDC vouchers launch claims
sections.summary: When the $130 million CDC vouchers were launched on 13 December, 550,000 households claimed within two days and 830,000 within 10 days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: On 13 December, when the $130 million CDC vouchers were launched by the Prime Minister, we were very, very heartened that within two days, 550,000 households claimed the vouchers; and within 10 days, 830,000 claimed.

sections.label: CDC voucher claims and spending
sections.summary: To date, 1.1 million Singaporean households have claimed the $100 CDC vouchers, with over $62 million spent in two and a half months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I just earlier mentioned that to date, 1.1 million Singaporean households have claimed the $100 CDC vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We are happy that over the last two and a half months, we have seen that more than $62 million of CDC vouchers have been spent.

sections.label: Merchant footfall increase
sections.summary: During Christmas, year-end and Lunar New Year, merchants reported footfall increased by an average of 20%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: If you remember – Christmas, year-end and then the Lunar New Year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We have heard from our merchants that, on average, their footfall has increased by 20%.

sections.label: Assurance Package CDC vouchers
sections.summary: Lawrence Wong announced that in January 2023 and January 2024, each Singaporean household will receive $200 of CDC vouchers, with major supermarkets included.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In addition, Minister Lawrence Wong announced that, come January 2023 and come January 2024, each Singaporean household will receive $200 of CDC vouchers as part of the Assurance Package, though for 2023 and 2024, the major supermarkets will be included in the list of participating merchants and hawkers.
